title: Numbering the notes
summary: Every note of a scale gets a number from 1 to 7: its scale degree.

steps.title: Scale degree
steps.body:
Each note of a scale has a number, counting up from the tonic: the tonic is 1, the next note is 2, and so on up to 7. These numbers are **scale degrees**.

**Why it matters:** Numbers work in any key. When your band says "start on the 3" or "go to the 5", they mean scale degrees, and you will use them all through Unit 5.

steps.title: Degrees in C major
steps.body: C is 1, D is 2, E is 3, F is 4, G is 5, A is 6, B is 7, and the top C is 1 again.

steps.title: Sing the numbers
steps.body: Play the C major scale and sing the numbers: 1 2 3 4 5 6 7 1. Then play a tune and try to name the degree of each note.
